CAN SCIENCE EXPLAIN GHOST?
Ghost sightings have been reported for centuries, yet science has not found
concrete proof of their existence. Some researchers believe these experiences can
be explained by psychology, such as sleep paralysis or heightened emotions. Others
point to environmental factors like electromagnetic fields. While science continues to
search for logical answers, many people still hold on to personal beliefs and cultural
stories. The debate between science and the supernatural reflects both human
curiosity and the desire to believe in the unknown.

Questions 19 to 26 are based on the following passage.
Read the passage carefully and choose the best answer A, B, C or D
For each question, mark your answer on the answer sheet.
As a student, I was disappointed in my family background. I had been
disturbed by my family's financial struggle since my first day in school. I could remember
how excited I was to be able to join my brother in primary school. He often told me the new
things that I could learn there. However, my father lost his job a few days before I was to
enter my Standard One and he was so devastated that he suggested that I stayed home
instead. I cried that day the whole day. I knew he had no choice as he had no money to pay
for my school fees and bus fare. My mother told me that I could help to look after my
younger siblings. She could then look for a job.
It was my aunt who came to my rescue. She pleaded with my parents and she offered
to pay for my education. I could never thank her enough even to this day. It was because of
her that I could go to school. However, I dared not ask too much from her. Throughout my
schooling years. I often faced the uncertainty of having enough money to further my
education.
My teachers and classmates did not make matters better for me. I was a plain-looking
girl with often hand-me-down uniforms. Everyone in school tended to favour pretty rich girls
who were more outspoken. Every year, I was passed over as a prefect or a monitor. I knew it
was because of my family background. As years passed, I became quieter and more ashamed
of my background. The only time when I could be proud of myself was during report card
day. That was when I got the admiration from my friends and praises from my teachers. The
best feeling was when I called my aunt to tell her my results.
My mother's health deteriorated when I was in Standard Six. I had to take over all the
household chores. As the only girl in the family, I felt that the burden of household chores
falling on me was unfair. Again, my father suggested that I stop school to take care of the
family. This time, my mother spoke up for me. I had the best results amongst my siblings. I
was glad that I did not have to stop schooling but my year-end examination result was bad
that year. I was placed in the last class in form one.
I had to struggle in Form One. Thank goodness, my mother recovered. Her
encouragement motivated me to not give up whenever I reached a breaking point. My
teachers were shocked with my year-end result. It was their first time seeing a student from
the last class performing so well. I was relieved when I was placed in the top class in form
two.

I finally realised my primary school dream of becoming a prefect when I was in form
three. It was my best year. My father was promoted and things were slightly better at home. I
could concentrate better in my studies. It was the year I had to sit for a public examination, so
I studied hard. When the result was announced at the end of the year, 1 scored straight As. I
was named the most outstanding student in the school that year. It was a very emotional
moment for me. My mother passed away a week before the award ceremony. She would have
been so proud to see me on stage.
I had a lot of disappointments throughout my school days, but those disappointments
made me stronger every day. As I look back, I realise how immature I had been for blaming
my father and my family background. I understand now that those were the experiences that
made me who I am today - a determined, confident lady. Every year, I never fail to visit and
thank my aunt. I am now the CEO of a company because my aunt sent me to school.
19. What was the effect on the family when the writer’s father lost his job?
A Her mother was forced to work by her father.
B The writer had to walk to school every day.
C All the children were unable to go to school.
D Her father did not have enough money to pay for her school fees.
20. What did the writer say about her aunt’s character?
A She was concerned about the writer's education.
B She was generous to pay throughout her schooling years.
C She was determined to take over the role of her parents.
D She was controlling and made sure the writer’s parents listened to her.
21. Why did the writer use the phrase best feeling?
A She was content with her results.
B She was proud of getting praises and being admired.
C She was excited to make her aunt happy and proud of her.
D She was happy that her result was better than the pretty rich girls’.

22. “ I felt that the burden of household chores falling on me was unfair”
What caused her to feel that way?
A She was mistreated by her father.
B She was tired of doing household chores.
C She had to take the whole responsibilities of the household chores.
D She did not have much time to study because of the household chores.
23. In the fifth paragraph the writer showed determination in her studies because
A Her mother was the main pillar that supported her.
B She wanted to impress the teachers
C She wanted to prove that a student from the last class could excel.
D She did not want to disappoint her mother.
24. Why did the writer feel emotional on the day she received her award?
A Regret of her family’s shortcomings.
B Proud of her outstanding achievement.
C Happy but very sad that her mother could not be there.
D Disappointed that her mother passed away a week before the award ceremony.
25. Why did the writer stop blaming her family background in the last paragraph?
A She is now determined and confident to be a CEO.
B She understands how difficult it had been for her father.
C She feels blessed to have an aunt who paid for education.
D She realises that it has made her determined to achieve success.
26. What does the writer want to highlight in the story?
A To argue that students should give up after disappointment.
B To emphasise on the importance of going to school.
C To focus on her struggles during her schooling years.

Titanic: A Remembrance
On 15 April, 1912, the largest passenger steamship ever built, appropriately named
Titanic, sank in the North Atlantic Ocean after hitting an iceberg. The Titanic had left
Southampton, England, five days earlier. It was her maiden voyage and her last.
In 1985, National Geographic Explorer-in-Residence Dr Robert Ballard located the
wreck of Titanic using a new deep sea underwater robot craft called Argo.
Earlier, he had asked the US Navy to finance Argo and they only agreed if he used it to find
two US nuclear submarines that had disappeared in the 1960s.
When Ballard and his team realised they had found Titanic, they jumped for joy. Then
they grasped the fact that they were celebrating something where people had died.
Ballard recalled, “I saw champagne bottles, intact, with the corks still in. The box
holding the bottles had disappeared long ago. Nearby I saw a
pair of smaller shoes that had perhaps belonged to a child. I felt that the people who had died
here in 1912 were speaking to me again.”
By then he knew that a private salvage company had legally removed
thousands of objects from the site. A Russian submarine had taken Hollywood filmmaker.
James Cameron to the wreck. A New York couple had even got married on Titanic’s bow.
He had asked people to treat Titanic’s remains with dignity.
“The story of Titanic is not about the ship, it’s about the people,” he said.

A Therefore they stopped work and held a memorial service.
B It was exactly what he did not want to happen.
C In 2004, Ballard went back to Titanic to see how it had changed.
D James Cameron’s film Titanic was a box-office hit.
E Suddenly, my eyes were drawn to a woman’s shoe.
F I realised so many people had lost their lives in that tragedy.
G Instead, they had turned her into a freak show.
H He was in fact on a secret mission for the US Navy when he found Titanic.

Ways to Reduce Air Pollution
A - Ginger, 16 years old
Since the introduction of air travel at the turn of the nineteenth century, this mode of
transportation has become one of the main contributors of the pollution problem. Undeniably,
air flights leave a massive carbon footprint in the atmosphere, but restricting air travel alone will
have little impact on curbing the air pollution problem.
B - Brian, 17 years old
In this era of globalisation, education is one of the mediums utilised by the governments of
many countries to enlighten the masses on the role that they have to play in reducing the air
pollution problem.
C - Carmel, 15 years old
Undeniably, increasing the price of fuels such as kerosene, petroleum and diesel is one of the
most effective ways to curb the air pollution problem as this would automatically reduce the
number of vehicles on the road. The exhausts of vehicles emit carbon dioxide and other noxious
gases that contaminate the air.
D - Mark, 16 years old
Reforestation is perhaps the best way to eliminate the presence of carbon dioxide from the
atmosphere. The segregation of forestland for the purpose of conservation can also help inhibit
air pollution.
E - Rahim, 17 years old
The government must take stern action on companies that carry out illegal logging in its stride
to curb the pollution problem. Heavy fines must be imposed on the wrongdoers. The Forestry
Department can step up security measures by conducting aerial surveillances and by assigning
more rangers to patrol the wooded area

F - Maria, 15 years old
I believe we can solve the air pollution problem by burying trash instead of burning it. As
responsible citizens, we must find ways and means to save planet Earth before it is too late.
